skills.name: Mode and mean from a frequency table

note.text:
When data are in a frequency table (values x, frequencies f):
• the mode is the value with the highest frequency;
• the mean = Σ(x × f) ÷ Σf: multiply each value by its frequency, add the products, then divide by the total frequency.
Example: number of brothers x: 0, 1, 2, 3 with frequencies f: 4, 6, 7, 3.
Mode: 2 (frequency 7). Σf = 20; Σ(x × f) = 0 + 6 + 14 + 9 = 29; mean = 29 ÷ 20 = 1.45.
Add a third column x × f to the table to organise the work.

worked_example.problem: Values {0}, {1}, {2}, {3} have frequencies {p}, {q}, {r}, {s}. Find the mode and the mean.
steps: Mode: the value with the highest frequency: {freqMode([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])}.
Σf = {freqTotal([p, q, r, s])}; Σxf = {freqSumXF([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])}; mean = {freqMean([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])}.
worked_example.answer: mode {freqMode([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])}, mean {freqMean([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])}

cards.idea: The mode is the value with the highest frequency.
example: Frequencies {3}, {8}, {5}: the mode is the value with {8}.

cards.idea: Σxf: multiply each value by its frequency and add.

check.prompt: Values 1, 2, 3, 4 have frequencies {p}, {q}, {r}, {s}. Find Σ(x × f).

misconceptions.explain: That is Σf; multiply each value by its frequency first.

check.prompt: Numbers of goals 0, 1, 2, 3 have frequencies {p}, {q}, {r}, {s}. Find the mean number of goals.

misconceptions.explain: Divide Σxf by the total frequency Σf, not by the number of values.

solution: Σf = {freqTotal([p, q, r, s])}; Σxf = {freqSumXF([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])}.
Mean = {freqSumXF([0, 1, 2, 3], [p, q, r, s])} ÷ {freqTotal([p, q, r, s])} = {answer}.
